cryptoTrack.accounts.unavailable: Connecting addresses is not ready yet.
cryptoTrack.assets.emptyTitle: Assets appear after the first read
cryptoTrack.assets.emptyHint: The app reads the network by itself: once the data arrives, the coins and tokens of the address are listed here. Operations are not entered by hand, the address is only read.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.title: {count} token awaits a decision | {count} tokens await a decision
cryptoTrack.quarantine.lead: These tokens came to the address on their own. Until you recognise them they are in neither the address's value, nor its profit, nor the reports, and do not count as capital.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.imitates: the name resembles a known token, the contract differs
cryptoTrack.quarantine.footnote: Tokens that are not on the recognised list stay out of the value and wait in quarantine, reviewed on this same tab.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.recognized: Token recognised and counted in the address's value
cryptoTrack.quarantine.hidden: Token hidden. You can bring it back in Settings, the Crypto subsection
cryptoTrack.quarantine.failed: Could not save the decision on the token
cryptoTrack.quarantine.whyAnyone: Anyone can send a token to your address: it costs pennies and needs no consent from you.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.whyFirst: So a new token waits in quarantine first: otherwise someone else's mailing would change your value, profit and reports.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.whyAfter: A recognised token counts like an ordinary asset. A hidden one is shown no more, and can be brought back in the section's settings.
cryptoTrack.quarantine.whyNotProtection: Quarantine does not protect the wallet: the app only reads the address and controls nothing in it. It protects your figures from other people's junk.
cryptoTrack.review.title: Recognise token {symbol}
cryptoTrack.review.counts: The token enters the address's value, its profit and the reports.
cryptoTrack.review.operations: Its transfers appear in the operations from {date}, the day the token arrived.
cryptoTrack.review.price: If providers have no price, the token counts as zero and is shown as a separate row.
cryptoTrack.review.contract: Contract {contract}. Check it in an explorer: a token's name can repeat a known one while the contract is a stranger's.
cryptoTrack.empty.title: No connected addresses yet
cryptoTrack.empty.body: Crypto does not have to be kept by hand. Connect a public address: the app reads the network itself, collects assets and operations and keeps them in an ordinary wallet. The address is only read: coins cannot be sent from the app, and no seed phrase or private key is needed.
cryptoTrack.empty.where: Create → Wallet → the Crypto kind. Networks, your own node and the consent are in Settings, the Crypto subsection.
cryptoTrack.connect.kindNote: The engine keeps a crypto wallet: the next step connects a public address on a network. The app only reads it, coins cannot be sent, and no seed phrase or private key is needed.
cryptoTrack.connect.title: Connect an address
cryptoTrack.connect.stepAddress: Step 2 of 3: the network and the public address.
cryptoTrack.connect.stepStart: Step 3 of 3: operations before this date are not loaded.
cryptoTrack.connect.consentLead: We ask once. After that the app refreshes the data by itself.
cryptoTrack.connect.consentNetwork: The public address goes to the network node (RPC) and to Blockscout: they will see the address and your IP. Prices come from DeFiLlama, and the address does not go there.
cryptoTrack.connect.consentReadOnly: The app reads balances and history. It cannot send or spend coins.
cryptoTrack.connect.consentStorage: The data lands in your vault and syncs only with devices at protection level 3.
cryptoTrack.connect.noSecretsTitle: We do not ask for a seed phrase or a private key
cryptoTrack.connect.noSecretsBody: There is nowhere to type them: neither the wizard nor the wallet page has a field for secrets. The consent can be withdrawn in Settings, the Crypto subsection; the data already collected stays in the vault.
cryptoTrack.connect.consentSaved: Consent saved. You can withdraw it in Settings, the Crypto subsection
cryptoTrack.connect.networkHint: We pull the coins and tokens of this network ourselves
cryptoTrack.connect.addressHint: Starts with 0x. Paste it from a wallet or an explorer: this is an address, not a key.
cryptoTrack.connect.addressInvalid: A public address is needed: 0x and 40 more characters 0-9 and a-f.
cryptoTrack.connect.refused: This looks like a seed phrase. We did not accept it and did not store it: paste the public address, it starts with 0x.
cryptoTrack.connect.refusedBody: The pasted text went neither to the vault nor to the network and was not written to any log. The app needs only a public address: a seed phrase and a private key give it nothing and cost you money. Never type them, here or in other apps.
cryptoTrack.connect.name: Name
cryptoTrack.connect.nameHint: To tell addresses apart in the list
cryptoTrack.connect.alreadyFollowed: This address is already connected on this network.
cryptoTrack.connect.nameTaken: A wallet with this name already exists, pick another.
cryptoTrack.connect.fromDateHint: The balance of that day is written as one opening adjustment
cryptoTrack.connect.wholeHistoryHint: Loads longer, but with no opening adjustment
cryptoTrack.connect.startDateHint: Usually the date from which you treat this address as yours
cryptoTrack.connect.startInvalid: Enter a real date, today or earlier.
cryptoTrack.connect.fromNote: The balance the address had on {date} is written as one opening adjustment. Operations before that date will not appear in the list, and profit is counted from it.
cryptoTrack.connect.wholeNote: The whole history of the address is loaded: there is no opening adjustment, and profit is counted from the first operation.
tour.wallet.cryptoOverview.title: A read-only address
tour.wallet.cryptoOverview.body: The network, the address and when it was last read. The app only reads the address: operations are not entered here and the balance is not corrected by hand.
tour.wallet.cryptoAssets.title: The address's assets
tour.wallet.cryptoAssets.body: Coins and tokens with quantity, price and share of the address's value. Only recognised tokens count.
tour.wallet.cryptoQuarantine.title: Quarantine
tour.wallet.cryptoQuarantine.body: Tokens that came to the address on their own wait for your decision. Recognise adds a token to the value and the reports, Hide removes it.
tour.stores.cryptoAdd.title: Connect an address
tour.stores.cryptoAdd.body: A public address on a network becomes an ordinary wallet: the app reads its assets and operations itself. No seed phrase or key is needed.
whatsNew.cryptoAddresses.title: Crypto addresses
whatsNew.cryptoAddresses.connect: Wallets → Connect an address: a public address on a network becomes a wallet of the Crypto kind. The app only reads it; it does not accept or store a seed phrase or a private key.
whatsNew.cryptoAddresses.quarantine: Tokens that came to the address on their own wait in quarantine under the assets table. Until you press Recognise, they are not in the value, the profit or the reports.
whatsNew.cryptoAddresses.readOnly: A wallet the engine drives has no buttons to create operations or correct the balance by hand: the data comes from the network.
cryptoTrack.review.undo: You can take the recognition back: the token returns to quarantine.
cryptoTrack.assets.takeBackBody: The token leaves the address's value, profit and reports and waits for your decision again. You can recognise it once more.
cryptoTrack.assets.takenBack: Token returned to quarantine and no longer counts towards the value
cryptoTrack.assets.takeBackFailed: Could not return the token to quarantine
